kinds.d: Dried or semi-dried fruit of the date palm, sold by cultivar, soft to firm.

x.d: Large, caramel-sweet cultivar from Morocco's Tafilalt, about 25% of world date trade.
Soft, pale, semi-transparent honey-flavoured date from Tolga, Algeria; leading date by export value.
Oval, dark-skinned date associated with Medina and eaten at iftar.
Tender, very sugary yellow to golden-brown date from Al-Qassim, Saudi Arabia.
Brown Gulf date regarded as the region's original cultivar; among the dearest Emirati dates.
Dark, soft Iranian date of 32-35% moisture, mainly eaten fresh rather than dried.

kinds.d: Dried grapes: dark raisins, golden sultanas and tiny dark Zante currants.

x.d: The common American sultana type, dried as dark raisins or treated with sulphur dioxide for golden raisins.
Small, dark, tart seedless dried grape; the name 'currant' comes from Corinth.
Larger and sweeter raisins from Muscat grapes.
Seedless raisin from the Flame grape.

kinds.d: Apricots dried whole or in halves, sulphured (orange) or unsulphured (dark, coarse).

x.d: Dried apricots from Malatya Province, which supplies roughly 95% of Turkey's output; Turkey overtook California as top producer.

kinds.d: Dried plums from European plum (Prunus domestica) varieties that dry without fermenting.
Figs dried in sun or ovens, including the Turkish Lob Injir sold as Calimyrna.

x.d: Smyrna-type fig needing caprifig pollination, Turkish Lob Injir brought to California in the late 19th century.

kinds.d: Sweetened dried cranberries and other berries, usually infused with sugar before drying.

x.d: Ocean Spray's registered trademark for sweetened dried cranberries, first seen in 1989 in a Ralston Purina cereal.

kinds.d: Dried mango, pineapple, papaya and banana chips; many are sugar-infused or candied before drying.

x.d: Dried carabao mango, a Cebu speciality made in the Guadalupe and Kalunasan areas of Cebu City.

kinds.d: Apples and pears dried as rings, slices or chips; sulphur dioxide is sometimes used to keep colour.

brands.d: Cranberry growers' cooperative founded 1930 as Cranberry Canners, named Ocean Spray in 1957; owner of the Craisins trademark.

notes: Pruneaux d'Agen IGP, Vostizza currants PDO, Aydın figs, Hunza and Blenheim apricots, d'Ente plum: no retrieved page confirmed them, so left out. Malaga muscatels merged as Muscat raisin (page describes Muscat raisins, not 'Malaga'). Candied fruit and nuts are in J8.
